messages:
alex_g: Heads up — seeing a flurry of redispatch churn in apac-gpu-pool over the last 10m. Fragmentation up ~12% and a couple of latency-sensitive tenants hit throttles. Cost signal spiked ~18% vs last hour. Pasting quick logs/snips below. :eyes:
ops-bot: [ALERT] redispatch-churn detected in apac-gpu-pool — eviction_count=23, avg_fragmentation=0.12, affected_tenants=[search-svc, experiments], severity=warning. Link: https://alerts/redwood/2141592653
maria_k: Can you paste the query + numbers? Need GPU-hour delta and which slabs/nodes are hot.
alex_g: Query I ran: `select node, free_gpus, fragmentation, tenant_count from pool_stats where pool='apac-gpu-pool' order by fragmentation desc limit 10`
Results (summary): node-gpu-23 free_gpus=0 frag=0.32 tenants=14; node-gpu-11 free_gpus=1 frag=0.28 tenants=9; node-gpu-02 free_gpus=0 frag=0.21 tenants=6. Forecasted delta_gpu_hours = +480 over next 24h if redispatch continues. Noticed 3 preemptions in last 5m (likely slab compaction).
samir: Sounds like slab compaction + aggressive redispatch. Proposal: increase slab_coalesce_window 30s -> 180s and throttle redispatch_rate temporarily. Also prefer spilling low-priority batch tenants to apac-burst pool. Quick sim?
jin: We can route non-latency batch tenants away with a rule: `route if tenant.labels.batch==true -> pool=apac-burst` I can canary 5% of batch traffic this afternoon.
maria_k: +1 to canary. Also want a hotfix: set redispatch_rate_limit to 25 req/min for 15m and watch. Who can push? :thumbsup:
alex_g: I can push that. Command: `infractl pool update apac-gpu-pool --redispatch-rate=25` Doing it now.
ops-bot: ops-bot: Deploy triggered by alex_g: infractl pool update apac-gpu-pool --redispatch-rate=25 — job_id=job-2141592653-1 — status: started.
alex_g: infractl returned job_id=job-2141592653-1 — update in progress. Initial metrics after change: eviction_count dropped 23 -> 6 in ~3m, fragmentation from 12% -> 8% (coarse).
maria_k: Nice drop. Forecast still high because of some hot tenants (search-svc). Can we enable prefix caching for search-svc to cut token throughput? That might shave GPU-hours.
samir: If caching saves 20-30% throughput we should fold that into the capacity model (Q2 forecast). Also run a sensitivity sim: prewarm vs eviction cost. Prewarm 4x GPU for 6h might be cheaper than repeated evictions.
jin: Prewarm command ready: `reservectl create --pool=apac-gpu-pool --count=4 --ttl=6h --tag=surge-hedge` I can spin that up on approval.
maria_k: Do it. Also schedule short follow-up in 2h. Action items: (1) alex: redispatch_rate_limit hotfix (done), (2) jin: reserve 4 nodes (in flight), (3) samir: simulate slab_coalesce change + report in 2h, (4) ops-runbook-bot: add runbook note under /runbooks/redispatch-frag.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook updated: /runbooks/redispatch-frag — mitigation steps added (hotfix rate-limit, burst spill, reserve hedge, slab_coalesce tuning).
alex_g: Reserve created by jin (id=reserve-2141592653-1), dashboard: https://console/redwood/pools/apac-gpu-pool/dash — eviction_count trending down. TL;DR: hotfix decreased churn, canary + reserve in progress, follow-up in 2h.
maria_k: Thanks. After canary, if slab_coalesce change looks good, schedule a 24h staggered rollout. We'll also update cost forecast and inform finance for Q2 repricing.
samir: I'll post sim results and a cost breakeven calc (prewarm vs eviction) in this thread.
jin: Canary started for batch spill -> apac-burst (5% traffic). Will report latency impact in 10m.
alex_g: Noted — will keep monitoring and escalate if anything regresses. Thanks everyone.
